title: Publish, update or stop sharing a map
summary: Publish the intended version and review what recipients can see.

evidence: server/src/utils/guideOracleKnowledge.js: reviewed original fact objects at b8345be4d2f7a097e81cb03eef64b473abd0cec9

sections.title: Publish the intended saved view
paragraphs: A Shared Map keeps the version explicitly published through Share. Editing the private map or saving its Studio presentation does not automatically change that snapshot.
steps: Open your own map and select the Studio view you intend to share.
Check that the design has saved, then open Share.
Review the notes and annotation settings intended for recipients.
Choose Publish share link for a first publication, or Update shared link to replace the published snapshot.

After publication or update completes, use Copy link and open that link in another browser tab to inspect the public version before sending it. If the design has newer unpublished changes, Copy existing link copies the earlier published version.
To stop sharing, reopen Share and select Unpublish. Wait for the private-map status before assuming the shared version is no longer available.
notes: Copying the existing link alone does not update its content.
Personal places are excluded from public Shared Maps. Owner prints and exports can include private planning content; check files separately.
An embedded presentation uses its published snapshot and omits resource-note rows. Preview the actual embed separately.
Unpublish starts from that button without an additional confirmation dialog. If publishing, updating or unpublishing reports an error, reopen Share and check its current status before retrying.

facts.title: Share a map
facts.message: Open your own map and review its sharing controls. A Shared Map is a view-only snapshot; update the shared version explicitly after changing your private map. Review what will be visible before sharing the link. You can stop sharing from the same controls.

sections.title: Saving versus publishing a resource on a Shared Map

facts.title: Saving versus publishing a resource on a Shared Map
keywords: save a place shared map automatically
saved resource appear on shared map
facts.message: Saving a Place or Programme/service adds it to your My Directory, not automatically to any My Map or Shared Map. Add that saved resource to the particular My Map you own. A published Shared Map is a separate snapshot: explicitly update the shared version and preview it before visitors can see the changed map. The Guide cannot add or publish it for you.

facts.title: Who opened a Shared Map
facts.message: The Guide cannot show who opened a Shared Map or identify viewers from chat. The reviewed My Map sharing controls let you inspect and update the published snapshot and stop sharing; I cannot verify an owner-facing viewer list or view-count report there. Review the content and link before sharing, and use Help to describe any reporting need without including other people’s details.

sections.title: Embed a Shared Map on a website

facts.title: Embed a Shared Map on a website
facts.message: From the Share controls of a published My Map, add an approved website, enable Website Embed, save the embed settings, and copy the embed code. The embedded presentation uses the published snapshot rather than unsaved map changes. Preview it and review guest-visible content before placing it on a website.

facts.title: Personal places and sharing
facts.message: Personal places are excluded from a published Shared Map. Your owner map and its resource-ledger downloads can include them, so review an export before sharing it with anyone. A personal place is not a public directory Place.
